symbols.name: armorx_handler_0B
symbols.evidence: handler 0x1e089e8 loads the immediate 0x32 into a 1-byte response buffer (b[sp+4] = 0x32) then jumps to the shared TX tail 0x1e08e5a with r1 = 0x0B == the opcode, confirming the case->opcode mapping. Live reply was A5 05 0B 30 E5 (payload 0x30 = 48) vs this immediate 0x32 = 50: the constant and the live value differ by 2 and the difference is NOT yet explained (FW-U-029)

symbols.name: armorx_handler_D6
symbols.evidence: 0x1e0921c reads [state+0x1b0], extracts the big-endian 16-bit value at record offset 2..3 (b[+3]<<8 | b[+2]) and replies with opcode 0xD6 via the shared TX builder 0x1e09426. NOTE: this contradicts the live-observed 144-byte D6 read - recorded as FW-U-028

symbols.name: armorx_handler_D7
symbols.evidence: 0x1e09232 copies len-4 payload bytes into a 144-byte staging buffer (sp+560), validates it with 0x1e0566a(length 0x90), then loops 4 times (r7 = 0..3) over record indices and calls 0x1e05c66 (record writer) when staging[0x70+i] differs; finishes with 0x1e069c2 and 0x1e059a2

symbols.name: armorx_handler_D8
symbols.evidence: 0x1e0928c takes payload[0..] as a 220-byte (0xDC) record validated by 0x1e0566a, selects the destination by payload[2] (b[r9+6]) into the record array [state+0x1b8] with stride 0xDC, and bounds-checks the index <= 0xDC

symbols.name: armorx_handler_D9
symbols.evidence: 0x1e09346 reads the 16-bit header word of record payload[0] (index < 4) from [state+0x1b8] with stride 0xDC and replies with opcode 0xD9 via 0x1e09426

symbols.name: armorx_crc16
symbols.evidence: CRC-16 routine: init 0xFFFF, LSB-first (reflected) nibble-table update, 16 halfword entries, returns low 16 bits. Matches the live-validated CRC-16/MODBUS (poly 0xA001, init 0xFFFF) used by the 144-byte config

symbols.name: armorx_record_header_validate
symbols.evidence: record-header validator: len = BE16 at [2..3]; rejects len<4 or len>max; computes 0x1e05628(ptr+2, len-2) and compares against the BE16 stored at [0..1]; prints 0x1e27206/0x1e27213 on mismatch

symbols.name: armorx_tx_tail
symbols.evidence: shared TX tail for the opcode/record replies

symbols.name: armorx_helper
symbols.evidence: record-index translation used by the D7 loop

symbols.name: armorx_helper
symbols.evidence: post-write finaliser called by the D7 path (stride/param handling)

symbols.name: armorx_frame_build
symbols.evidence: writes magic 0xA5 (0x1e05dc4) and flips to 0xA4 when the payload exceeds capacity-4 (0x1e05dd6); computes nfrags = (len+2)/(capacity-5) (0x1e05dda-0x1e05de4). This is the A5-vs-A4 framing rule.

symbols.name: armorx_frame_checksum_sum8
symbols.evidence: sum8 loop: r3 = b[r0++]; r2 += r3; return r2.l. Every frame in the live D7/D6 transaction log satisfies it.

symbols.name: transport_send
symbols.evidence: library send called directly after 0x1e0642c in 0x1e09426; result stored at [r8+0x158].

symbols.name: armorx_response_send_direct
symbols.evidence: direct-send fallback of 0x1e0642c (called when no queue entry is free).

symbols.name: armorx_tx_frame_magic_check
symbols.evidence: TX path reads b[frame+0] and requires 0xA5 (0x1e064b4) or A4 (0x1e064ce/0x1e064d4), then reads the fragment ordinal at frame[3] (0x1e064da).
